_comment: Reaction templates of the organic network generator (src/reaction_templates.rs, src/network_generator.rs). A template is a graph transformation, not a reaction: each reactant slot is a list of SMARTS alternatives (the first atom of every alternative is the reacting atom, atom i of an alternative means the same thing in all of them), `edits` rewrite the matched atoms (op: break | bond | set_bond between two atoms (slot, pattern atom), charge, h_delta), and the products are the connected pieces of the result. The rate comes from rate rules in the manner of RMG: the matching rule of the highest specificity (the number of constraints in its `when` conditions) gives the pre-exponential factor and activation energy, and every matching modifier scales them (a_factor, ea_add_kj; `per_match` counts the occurrences of its pattern, `unless` excludes). A condition is `{reactant, center, smarts}` (the pattern's first atom is the atom matched by pattern atom `center` of that reactant's slot) or `{solvent: [classes]}`. `degeneracy` multiplies the rate by the number of hydrogens on an atom (statistical factor). Catalysts are species whose concentration enters the rate law with the given order. Nothing here names a compound: a new reaction type is a new entry. K is never stated: it comes from the formation data of reactants and products (a reaction whose species lack data is irreversible). Every number is a recalled literature value or a class estimate, tier Estimated; the source of each is on its rule. Added in the sixth pass: Diels-Alder, Friedel-Crafts alkylation and acylation (the Lewis acid is a catalyst species of the rate law), organomagnesium halide addition and protonolysis, Wittig olefination.
